back: Effusive: runny, low-viscosity lava flows out (shield volcanoes). Explosive: viscous, gas-rich magma is blasted into ash and fragments (stratovolcanoes).
Stratovolcano: steep cone of lava and ash. Shield: broad, runny basalt. Cinder cone: small cone of fragments. Lava dome: mound of viscous lava. Fissure: lava sheets from long cracks.
A fast avalanche of hot gas, ash and rock at several hundred degrees Celsius, travelling at over 100 km/h: the most lethal volcanic hazard.
A volcanic mud flow of ash and water (rain, melted ice or a crater lake) that follows valleys and can travel tens of kilometres.
A sudden flood caused by an eruption melting a glacier or ice cap (Iceland).
A scale from 0 to 8 based mainly on erupted volume and column height; roughly logarithmic, with each step about ten times the volume.
VEI 6 eruption in the Philippines; about 800 deaths because of warnings and evacuation; sulfur dioxide cooled the global climate by about 0.5 °C for about two years.
A VEI 3 eruption in Colombia: lahars from melted ice buried Armero and killed about 23 000 people, as the warnings were not acted on in time.
Fertile soils, jobs in farming and tourism, geothermal energy, poverty, family ties, and underestimating rare risks.
